observations: A large rounded head fills the center, covered in overlapping yellow, teal, dark red, and olive color blocks, with a flat-topped black hat outlined in thick yellow along the top edge.
Two mismatched eyes: the left is a wide circular socket with zebra-striped marks and a blue iris; the right is smaller, white-outlined, with radiating lines and an open stare.

Two white-outlined hands appear at lower left and lower right, filled with dark red lines; a row of white rectangular teeth runs across the lower face, and loose teal and blue lines scatter across the surface.
reading: The hat sits as a flat structural cap above a face pulled in several directions — yellow on the right side, cold teal and dark red on the left. The two eyes refuse to match, giving the head an off-balance alertness. Hands at the edges read as either greeting or warning. Loose scattered lines cross the solid color blocks without resolving into either.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, title neighbors are nnxyz nnotb #293 and nnxyz nnotb #295. All three place a large head against a plain ground with raised hands and exposed teeth, but #294 is the only one in this owned group where a hat functions as a dominant structural element.

connections.reason: nnxyz nnotb #293 shares the open-mouth teeth row and mismatched eye treatment, but replaces the dark layered palette with bright pastels on a deep blue ground, making the two a direct warm-versus-cool contrast.
nnxyz nifty faces #108 uses dense overlapping line-scribble across a large central head with a prominent teeth row, though its palette is far more saturated and its ground is grey rather than dark.

lookingQuestion: The two eyes are drawn with different shapes, sizes, and marks — what does that difference do to how you read the direction the figure is facing?
ambiguities: The loose teal and blue lines crossing the face may be separate drawn marks or outlines for underlying color areas; image resolution does not resolve this.
The yellow and blue marks inside the hat top are ambiguous — possibly a decorative element, a reflected line, or an unrelated mark.
